learningObjective: Identify legitimate motivations for loop fission and cases where fission is counter-productive.

canonicalClaims.claim: Loop fission splits one loop body into two loops sharing the same iteration space, motivated by (a) relieving register pressure, (b) exposing vectorization / parallelization on a subset of statements, and (c) allowing different tile sizes or schedules per half.
conditions: The dependence graph after fission remains acyclic (no forward-crossing dependences created).
The two halves can each be scheduled independently.
nonImplications: Does not imply any single fission decision is always a wall-clock win.
Does not imply fission is semantics-fixing; it is semantics-preserving only when legal.

misconceptions.claim: Loop fission improves cache behavior whenever the original body reuses intermediate values within an iteration.
misconceptions.whyWrong: That scenario is the classic case for fusion, not fission; fission would force the intermediate to be materialized across iterations.

misconceptions.claim: Fission can reorder side-effecting operations to fix a buggy program.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Fission is semantics-preserving only when the dependence graph permits it; it does not change program meaning.

misconceptions.claim: Fission is always legal because it does not change the iteration space.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Fission is legal only if the dependence graph between the two halves is acyclic; otherwise it violates cross-statement dependences.

misconceptions.claim: Fission is the same as unrolling, since both replicate loop bodies.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Unrolling replicates the body across consecutive iterations; fission splits statements into separate loops across the same iteration space.

implementationFacts: Polyhedral compilers (e.g., MLIR affine loop distribution) use fission followed by fusion to reshape loop nests.
Halide's schedule split_loop / distribute achieves fission on TensorIR-style pipelines.
performanceScenarios: A 20-statement inner body with many live scalars can be fissioned into two 10-statement bodies to reduce register pressure and enable vectorization.
